newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Recount confirms nationalist victories in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Recount confirms nationalist victories in Bosnia.

text.p: A recount of Bosnia's election results after errors were discovered has confirmed nationalist party victories in races for a new parliament and regional assemblies, organisers said on Monday.

The "preliminary final results" must still be re-verified by computer and opened to possible appeal before they can be officially certified, expected by next weekend, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe said.

President Alija Izetbegovic's Moslem SDA party amassed 54 percent of the vote for the 28 out of 42 seats in the Bosnian House of Representatives reserved for candidates running in Bosnia's Federation (Moslem-Croat) entity.
The Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ), Bosnian wing of Croatia's ruling nationalist party, was next with 25.3 percent, followed by the moderate Joint List coalition at 7.9 percent.
Former prime minister Haris Silajdzic's moderate Party for Bosnia-Herzegovina (SBiH) finished fourth at seven percent.
In voting for 14 House seats allotted to candidates running in Bosnia's Serb Republic entity, the area's dominant nationalist Serb Democratic Party (SDS) took 54.5 percent.
SDA candidates backed by Moslem war refugees from Serb territory garnered 17.2 percent and the relatively moderate Serb Union for Peace and Progress (SMP) was third at 12.8 percent.
The far rightist Serbian Radical Party tallied 5.8 percent.
The SDS cruised to an absolute majority in the new 83-seat Serb Republic assembly with 52.3 percent. The refugee-backed SDA finished a strikingly strong second at 16.3 percent.
Analysts said the need for SDA deputies to travel into Serb territory and work at close quarters with anti-Moslem Serbs may pose security problems for international peace coordinators.
The SMP coalition took 11.5 percent of the vote and the Serbian Radical Party got 6.6 percent.
Polling for the 140-seat Federation assembly gave the SDA 54 percent, the HDZ 24.5 percent, the Joint List 7.9 percent and the SBiH 7.3 percent.
In the Serb Republic's presidential race, acting entity president Biljana Plavsic of the SDS accumulated 59 percent followed by SDA refugee candidate Adib Dozic at 17.4 percent.
The OSCE earlier announced that Izetbegovic narrowly beat SDS challenger Momcilo Krajisnik for the senior seat of a new Bosnian inter-ethnic presidency.
Izetbegovic is to be effective head of state for the next two years, with Krajisnik and Croat Kresimir Zubak taking the other two seats on the presidency.
The SDA was expected to get roughly 20 seats in the Bosnian House of Representatives, the SDS eight or nine with the HDZ and a few small parties rounding out the picture.
The presidency must govern by consensus and the legislatures by majority quorum.
